children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures closed higher for a second session as another round of spikes in crude oil spilled over into the Canadian oilseed.

However, that support Thursday wasn't enough for the other vegetable oils. Chicago soybeans and soyoil, along with European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil, were lower on the day. Only Chicago soymeal chalked up a small increase.

Saskatchewan reported its canola harvest was 26% complete, up 11 points on the week. Combining provincewide reached 41% done, half of the five-year average. Humid and wet conditions continued to slow field progress.
Prairie temperatures have been forecast to range from the mid teens to mid-20s Celsius with little to no rain heading into the weekend, which will help combining.
Southern Manitoba and parts of central Alberta are expected to get precipitation during the weekend.
The Canadian dollar fell further to 70.71 U.S. cents compared to Wednesday's close of 70.94.
There were 60,187 canola contracts traded on Thursday, compared to 59,825 on Wednesday. Spreading accounted for 39,002 contracts traded.
